transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-11 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 52m
- Attendees: Alex Marin (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dylan Reyes (Redwood Solutions); Marcus Liu (CTO), Elena Park (ML Platform), Jonas Mendez (Security), Rita Gomez (SRE)

Auto-generated summary: scoped dedicated capacity needs for an early pilot, key compliance asks (SOC2, KMS), and next steps for pricing and benchmark.

---
00:00 Alex Marin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Alex from Redwood, i run the west AE book. quick intro round then we'll jump into your capacity goals and constraints.
00:18 Marcus Liu: Hi, Marcus here CTO at Solace. thanks. we're interested in moving from hosted evals to dedicated pools for inference — main drivers are latency predictability and data isolation for clinical note generation.
00:35 Elena Park: hi all, Elena — we run the ML infra. our current stack is GKE + internal message bus, models are Llama-2 family variants right now and some finetuned t5-ish rerankers. Average sequence length is 512 tokens, bursts up to 400 concurrent requests for critical routes.
00:55 Priya Shah: thanks. couple quick clarifying q's: when you say 400 concurrent, is that steady qps or short spikes? and what's the target p95 latency?
01:06 Elena Park: mostly short spikes, like 30-90s spikes triggered by product events, peak qps around 400 but average is ~60. Target p95 ~250-300ms for text gen at 512 tokens.
01:20 Dylan Reyes: that p95 at 512 is a useful anchor. our Dedicated pools can be configured with prewarmed "hot" instances (hot pool) and we can reserve capacity to guarantee baseline throughput, plus burst capacity that either prewams or momentarily borrows from a shared pool depending on plan.
01:39 Marcus Liu: what's the difference operationally between prewarm hot pool vs. borrowing spare capacity? how does that affect cost and isolation?
01:48 Priya Shah: good question — two modes: 1) hot pool = reserved GPUs that are kept warm, isolated to your tenant, predictable cost and latency. 2) burst borrow = we route to a lower-tier pool; lower isolation, slightly higher variance in latency and requires fallback logic. For regulated clinical text we recommend hot pool for the critical routes.
02:10 Jonas Mendez: from security perspective we need VPC-only egress, customer-managed KMS, and full audit logs. also SOC2 compliant controls and SSO (SAML) for the console. can you support HSM or bring-your-own-key?
02:24 Priya Shah: yes — we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, HSM integrations for enterprise & Private, and we can provide detailed audit logs. our SOC2 docs are in the security pack, we'll share the standard package and a higher-compliance addendum.
02:40 Rita Gomez: on networking — we will want strict VPC peering, no public egress for inference traffic, and egress rules locked down. what does setup look like and how long does it take?
02:52 Alex Marin: typical VPC setup for Dedicated is 2-5 business days to provision peering and firewall policies once order's signed, sometimes longer for strict enterprise network reviews. we'll include a network runbook.
03:05 Elena Park: about sizing — our worst-case is sustained 400 concurrent for a minute or two, then drops. can you walk through how to model reserved GPU count for that?
03:18 Priya Shah: sure. we ask for representative traces and the prompt set. sizing is a function of model throughput (tokens/sec per GPU at your batch size), shaped by quantization and sequence length. ballpark: for Llama-2-13B quant 4bit you might get ~120-150 tokens/sec per A100-class equivalent; at 512 tokens and your p95 target you'd need N GPUs — we'll run a small perf run to nail the numbers.
03:42 Marcus Liu: we also run rerankers and a dense-embedding pipeline. can the Dedicated pool isolate GPU memory per tenant? what's tenant fencing look like?
03:52 Priya Shah: Dedicated has tenancy modes: full-node isolation — entire GPU nodes dedicated to you; and vshare where multiple tenants share nodes but with nvlink noop? (note: transcription may be off) For PHI workloads we push for full-node isolation. we can show a tenancy matrix in the runbook.
04:15 Dylan Reyes: there's also an option to pin model variants to the reserved pool and route less sensitive workloads to hosted fallback models automatically when dedicated is overloaded — so you get isolation for core flows and a cost-optimized fallback.
04:31 Elena Park: how does automatic fallback affect observability and tracing? we need request attribution across the fallback for debugging.
04:40 Priya Shah: we inject trace headers and propagate request IDs. the Console will show per-route model and latency breakdown. if a request falls back we tag it in the logs and in traces so you can see whether it hit the dedicated or hosted tier.
04:58 Marcus Liu: pricing: what's the delta between full-node reservation vs shared burst credits?
05:05 Alex Marin: full-node reservation is priced as committed capacity (monthly) — predictable but higher baseline. burst credits let you keep a smaller committed footprint and pay for spikes; however cost-per-token during bursts is higher. i'll share a tiered pricing sheet that lays out examples for your traffic shape.
05:24 Jonas Mendez: regulatory question: can we run an on-prem/private deployment? we may need an air-gap for certain envs.
05:32 Priya Shah: yes we have a Private offering (VPC/on-prem) — deployment times are longer and there's a platform fee. for air-gapped we do an on-prem package; we can discuss support model.
05:45 Elena Park: about burst strategy — we prefer not to overcommit capacity for cost reasons. want a mix: reserved baseline for critical routes, small hot pool, and an automated shedding policy for non-critical requests. does Redwood offer shedding rules by route/priority?
06:00 Dylan Reyes: yes — you can define per-route SLAs and priority. non-critical routes can be configured to queue, throttle, or route to hosted cheaper variants. we also have a canary rollouts and A/B traffic split features for model upgrades.
06:16 Marcus Liu: for pilot can we run a smoke test with our prompt set and a synthetic traffic profile to reproduce spikes?
06:22 Priya Shah: absolutely — that's standard. priya will send the benchmark checklist and a k6 script sample. we recommend 3-day pilot with traffic bursts to simulate events.
06:33 Rita Gomez: how do we handle KV cache and cold-starts for autoregressive models? we've seen big latency hits on cold kv lookups.
06:42 Priya Shah: we have prefix caching and KV-aware prewarm. for models where KV cache is critical we recommend warming sequences or keeping a warm hot-pool; caching reduces incremental token cost and p95. also note that very aggressive quantization can impact cache hit behavior slightly — we'll include best practices.
07:05 Elena Park: any constraints on model families? we use a custom finetune of Llama-2-13B and a small Mistral for chat-like flows.
07:14 Priya Shah: we support major open families; for custom finetunes we help onboard weights and run a validation pass. quantized variants are possible; sometimes we recommend a mixed approach (quant for non-critical, fp16 for critical).
07:29 Marcus Liu: SLA questions: what are realistic latency SLAs for 95th at our target sizes?
07:36 Dylan Reyes: we provide SLA tiers; for dedicated with hot-pools and pinned models you can get p95 latency SLOs of ~200-300ms for 512 tokens depending on model. SLOs are defined per-plan and tied to reserved capacity.
07:50 Jonas Mendez: audit logs — are they immutable and for how long? retention options?
07:56 Priya Shah: we provide immutable audit logs with configurable retention; standard retention 90 days, enterprise options for longer and export hooks to your SIEM.
08:08 Marcus Liu: okey. i also want to understand failure modes. if a whole AZ has an outage, how does Dedicated fail over?
08:17 Dylan Reyes: failover depends on your Dedicated topology: multi-AZ reserved pools replicate capacity and we can failover to a different AZ or route to Hosted fallback. there's an RTO/RPO tradeoff; we can design cross-AZ replication for critical flows.
08:34 Elena Park: one more thing — developer experience: we need SDKs and sample infra templates for k8s sidecars to call Redwood endpoints with mutual TLS.
08:44 Alex Marin: we have client SDKs (python, js, go) and k8s helm charts for sidecars; Priya will share code snippets.
08:51 Marcus Liu: any known limitations for GPU types? we prefer A100 but open to H100 for cost/perf tradeoffs.
08:58 Priya Shah: both supported; H100 yields higher throughput for some models but has different quant/kernel tradeoffs. we'll include reference perf numbers for both.
09:12 Dylan Reyes: quick note on billing — token-based metering plus committed capacity charges. burst billing is hourly or per-burst unit. we'll model a 30 day projected spend in the pricing sheet.
09:24 Elena Park: ok great. i want to flag data residency: we need EU-only processing for a subset. does Redwood support region pinning?
09:33 Priya Shah: yes region pinning is supported; you can restrict models and routes to EU regions. Dedicated can be provisioned in specific regions to satisfy residency.
09:41 Marcus Liu: sounds good. next steps recap please.
09:45 Alex Marin: recap: Alex sends pricing & SLA examples by Fri; Priya sends benchmark checklist + k6 by Mon; customer provides prompt set and perf targets by mid-next week; we aim to schedule pilot for week of 2026-03-23.
09:59 Elena Park: perfect. thanks all.
10:02 Jonas Mendez: thanks, bye.
10:06 Alex Marin: thanks team — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.

(Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions of product names — e.g., "hot pool" sometimes rendered as "hotpol" or "kv cash" instead of KV cache. Some speaker labels may switch between full names and generic. Natural pauses and overlapping speech present.)
